Definition: to parch (through drought) i.e. (by analogy,) to desolate, destroy, kill
BiblicalUsage: Charab is laying waste, desolating, and it is the word of Assyria's trail and of God's judgment alike. The kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and cast their gods into the fire, Ezekiel says the cities shall be laid waste and the high places desolate, Amos hears that the high places of Isaac shall be desolate, and the cities that are inhabited shall be laid waste.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe desolation in Scripture is never the last word, but it is a true word: empires waste nations, and God wastes the altars His people built to false gods. I hold that the same God who lays waste also promises to rebuild, and I read these verses with both halves in view.
